source1: Krishnendu Ray, 'Khadga Dynasty', Banglapedia: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh, Asiatic Society of Bangladesh, 2012 - https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Khadga_Dynasty
source2: A.M. Chowdhury, 'Samatata', Banglapedia: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh, Asiatic Society of Bangladesh, 2012 - https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Samatata
notes: Last securely attested king Balabhata (c.690-705). Sources say only that the Deva dynasty 'may have supplanted' the Khadgas in the 8th century; no evidence on how or when Khadga rule ended. Database end 700 is approximate.

source2: Amira K. Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires, Edinburgh University Press, 2016 (publisher description) - https://edinburghuniversitypress.com/book-the-almoravid-and-almohad-empires.html
notes: Almohad revolt began 1121 among Masmuda Berbers of the High Atlas, Almoravid subjects, so internal under brief; they took Marrakesh 1147, ending the state. Andalusi revolts 1144-45. External reading (T2) arguable.

successor: Herakleopolitan kingdom (9th/10th Dynasties), Period of the Regions
source2: J.-D. Stanley, M.D. Krom, R.A. Cliff and J.C. Woodward, 'Nile Flow Failure at the End of the Old Kingdom, Egypt', Geoarchaeology 18(3), 2003 - https://www.research.manchester.ac.uk/portal/files/24322095/POST-PEER-REVIEW-PUBLISHERS.PDF
notes: Central authority weakened, nomarchs became autonomous; Old Kingdom 'collapsed into anarchy' c.2160 BCE amid famine; throne passed to Herakleopolitan kings, Thebes a rival. No foreign conquest. Chronologies vary (Britannica ends Dyn 8 c.2118).

source1: Klaus Schippmann, 'Arsacids ii. The Arsacid dynasty', Encyclopaedia Iranica II/5, 1986 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/arsacids-ii
source2: Josef Wiesehöfer, 'Ardašīr I i. History', Encyclopaedia Iranica II/4, 1986 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ardasir-i
notes: Ardashir, 'a minor Parthian vassal in Persis', rebelled, killed Artabanus IV in battle 28 April 224, crowned c.226. Rebel vassal counts as internal, so T1c not T2. Civil war Vologases VI vs Artabanus IV from c.213.

Rashtrakutas defeated the Chalukyas (Dantidurga c.753); Kirtivarman II 'replaced' 757. Rashtrakutas were Chalukya feudatories (standard view, not stated in opened sources), so internal: T1c. Database 753 marks Dantidurga's victory, not final end.

successor: Seleucid Empire (Seleucus I), then Ptolemy Keraunos (Macedon)
notes: After execution of heir Agathocles (c.283/282) and ensuing disorder, Seleucus I invaded, killed Lysimachus at Corupedium 281 BCE and annexed his realm; murdered near Lysimacheia by Ptolemy Keraunos. Home area 'Konya Plain' odd; capital in Thrace.
